name: Poolz LockedDeal CreateMassPools integer overflow
summary: LockedDeal.CreateMassPools(address,uint64[],uint256[],address[]) charges the caller getArraySum(_StartAmount), and getArraySum accumulates the caller-supplied array with an unchecked sum = sum + _array[i] under Solidity 0.6.12. An amount array summing to 1 modulo 2**256 therefore transferred a single token unit in while CreatePool credited the attacker's pools with the full element values, and because the pools' _FinishTime was already past, WithdrawToken immediately paid out the contract's entire balance of each token.
notes: LockedDeal was created top-level in this transaction and its runtime is immutable: the same 23614-character runtime and keccak hash appear at the creation block, at block 26475366 immediately before the exploit, and in the anchor transaction prestate.

Exact token depletion of LockedDeal 0x8bfaa473a899439d8e07bf86a8c6ce5de42fe54b on BSC, summed from the ERC20 Transfer logs whose sender is the contract across the five exploit transactions between blocks 26475367 and 26475466. Every component is a thin PancakeSwap listing that the attacker's own selling moved, so each is valued at realised proceeds, not spot: the per-token unitPriceUsd is the BNB the attacker EOA actually received when selling that token, at the DefiLlama BNB price of 311.7638042244487 at the anchor timestamp, divided by the quantity taken. Realised proceeds total 1328.5787180093985 BNB. PORTX realises zero because the attacker burned all of it to the zero address at block 26490195 after failing to sell it, and part of the KMON was never sold, so the total is a floor. The Ethereum and Polygon deployments of the same contract were drained in the same hour by the same attacker; those losses belong to their own records and are excluded here, which is why this figure is not PeckShield's ~$390,000 cross-chain estimate.
